title: What is the highest common factor of numbers next to each other?
description: Five pairs of numbers that sit next to each other are tried: eight and ten, fourteen and sixteen, nine and eleven, fifteen and seventeen, twelve and thirteen. A common factor must go into the gap between the numbers, which explains the pattern. Keeko doubts this and thinks nine and eleven also give two.
teaching_notes: One idea: a common factor of two numbers also goes into the gap between them, so numbers two apart share at most two and numbers one apart share only one. Watch for students who say two for every pair that is two apart, even when the numbers are odd.

source: Find the HCF of 8 and 10, 14 and 16, 9 and 11, 15 and 17, and 12 and 13. State what you notice.
video_script.why: The child can find a highest common factor and now looks for a pattern across five pairs that sit next to each other.
video_script.substitution: A common factor goes into both numbers, so it also goes into the gap between them, which limits the highest common factor.
video_script.anchor: The five pairs written in a column: 8 and 10; 14 and 16; 9 and 11; 15 and 17; 12 and 13.
video_script.wrong_answer: so the highest common factor is two too
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko thinks nine and eleven are two apart, so the highest common factor is two too, but two does not go into odd numbers.
video_script.payoff_line: Even numbers next to each other have the highest common factor two

final_answer.value: Even numbers next to each other: HCF 2; odd numbers next to each other: HCF 1; numbers next to each other: HCF 1
final_answer.spoken: two for even numbers and one for odd numbers

hold_back: Even numbers next to each other: HCF 2
never_show: 2 as the HCF of 9 and 11, marked right
maths_rules: 9 and 11: HCF 1; 15 and 17: HCF 1; 12 and 13: HCF 1
a common factor of two numbers also divides the gap between them: 3 divides 9 and 15 and also 15 - 9 = 6
even pairs two apart: the gap is 2, so a common factor is 1 or 2, and 2 divides both, so the HCF is 2
odd pairs two apart: the common factor is 1 or 2, but 2 does not divide odd numbers, so the HCF is 1
numbers one apart: the gap is 1, so the HCF is 1
slip: 9 and 11 are two apart, but 2 does not divide 9, so the HCF is 1, not 2

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step one, take eight and ten, and then fourteen and sixteen. Each pair is two apart.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>A common factor must go into two, so it is one or two.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Both numbers of each pair are even, so two goes in. The highest common factor of each pair is two.

<bookmark mark='m2'/>But the numbers are odd, and two does not go into odd numbers.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>The only common factor is one, so the highest common factor of each pair is one.

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Keeko thinks nine and eleven are two apart, so the highest common factor is two too.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>But two goes only into even numbers, and nine and eleven are odd.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>A common factor must go into both numbers, so two cannot work. The answer stays one.
